title: Acceleration traction force
description: Essential: Correctly calculates the traction force during acceleration using Newton's second law, F = ma + 0.05mg.

title: Maximum acceleration speed
description: Important: Correctly applies the power relationship P = Fv to find the speed v1 at the end of the constant acceleration phase.

title: Acceleration time
description: Essential: Correctly calculates the acceleration duration using kinematics (t = v1 / a) to obtain the final answer of 20 s.

title: Maximum driving speed
description: Essential: Correctly calculates the maximum speed at constant velocity using force equilibrium (P = f * vm) to obtain the final answer of 20 m/s.

title: Hydrogen mass calculation
description: Essential: Correctly applies energy conservation with efficiency to calculate the required hydrogen mass, obtaining the final answer of 12.6 kg.

title: Energy-work equivalence
description: Important: Correctly relates the engine's useful work output to the work done against resistance over the 300 km distance.

title: Unit consistency
description: Optional: Demonstrates consistent unit handling, particularly converting km to m and kW to W.

title: Incorrect force balance
description: Pitfall: Uses only ma or only 0.05mg for the traction force during acceleration, omitting the other term.

title: Power formula misuse
description: Pitfall: Misapplies P = Fv, e.g., using the acceleration force to find maximum speed or vice-versa.

title: Efficiency error
description: Pitfall: Misplaces the 50% efficiency factor, either applying it to the resistance work or the fuel energy incorrectly.
